terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Observed as a floor-standing railway crew attendance terminal. Front interaction zones are reference-grounded; hidden rear and full side surfaces are low-poly approximations.

reasoning: The shell is composed of multiple stepped and sloped hard-surface masses rather than one cuboid.
The recognition recess and movable arm require a nested action-ready hierarchy.
Vent perforations and keyboard keycaps are repeated systems that affect identity at close range.
The main screen, white shell, gray interface fascia, black worktop, keyboard and blue connectors require distinct material responses.
The single oblique view and foreground occlusion create high hidden-side uncertainty.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Narrow real chamfers on white shell edges.
Tall black sensor bay with a dark perimeter channel.
Circular pivot cap on the articulated recognition arm.
Broad low-roughness reflection on screen glass.
Recessed camera lens cavity in the top housing.
Two aligned recessed card slots below the screen.
Grouped circular sockets in the gray interface fascia.
Paired blue caps with raised radial grip ribs.
Broad low-roughness reflection on black worktop.
Bounded six-row repeated keycap system with touchpad.
Dedicated fingerprint sensing patch and semantic label.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the front-oblique training camera, the model must read immediately as the supplied attendance kiosk rather than a generic terminal.

The sloped white shell, large inset screen, left recognition recess with articulated arm, dual card-slot module, gray connector fascia and black worktop must preserve their observed relative positions.
The model must stay within a 12000-triangle target for the complete kiosk, with vent holes and keycaps implemented as bounded repeated systems.
Main screen, worktop, painted shell, interface plastics, keyboard and blue connector caps must remain visually distinct under neutral and grazing light.
Clickable component groups must include screen, recognition arm, dual card-slot module, keyboard, fingerprint zone and connector panel.

featureGroups.name: Stepped shell silhouette and front operating depth
qualityCriteria: The top screen housing, recessed connector fascia, projecting worktop and lower cabinet form four readable depth steps.
The main screen remains the dominant front mass while the worktop projects far enough to support keyboard interaction.
failureModes: the cabinet collapses into a single rectangular box
screen housing, fascia and worktop sit on one plane
the main screen is too small relative to the white shell

featureGroups.name: Recognition recess and articulated arm
qualityCriteria: A tall black inset recess sits to the operator-left of the main screen.
The recognition arm pivots from the recess and projects horizontally across the front face.
The arm has a visible circular joint cap and a rectangular sensor head.
failureModes: the recess is replaced by a flat decal
the arm floats without a pivot socket
the arm is omitted or placed on the wrong side of the main screen

featureGroups.name: Front card-slot and connector modules
qualityCriteria: The dual black card-slot module is inset below the screen and contains two aligned slots.
The gray connector fascia contains separated circular ports, two blue capped connectors and vent perforation groups.
Every raised module has a named parent socket, overlap and local transform.
failureModes: the card-slot module floats above the shell
the two blue connector caps merge into one shape
front ports are distributed randomly instead of grouped by the reference

featureGroups.name: Worktop, keyboard and fingerprint interaction zone
qualityCriteria: The black worktop is a separate glossy slab projecting toward the operator.
The keyboard contains a bounded repeated key grid plus a distinct touchpad region.
The fingerprint interaction zone remains a separate clickable patch on the operator-right side.
failureModes: keyboard is painted into the worktop rather than modeled as a component
key repetition exceeds the mobile triangle budget
fingerprint zone has no separate interaction anchor

featureGroups.name: Kiosk material separation and controlled look development
qualityCriteria: Warm-white painted shell, black screen glass, black glossy worktop, gray fascia, metallic keyboard and cyan-blue connector caps remain distinct.
Reference PBR evidence reaches confidence >= 0.7 for every admitted material crop used as implementation evidence.
Neutral and grazing-angle views prove that screen and worktop reflections do not erase component boundaries.
failureModes: white shell, gray fascia and black worktop collapse to one roughness response
screen reads as matte paint instead of glass-like material
blue connector caps lose their color separation under neutral light

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Overall dimensions are ratio-based and use an approximate 2.1 meter standing terminal height.
Hidden rear and right-side surfaces use plain powder-coated panels with no unobserved service hardware.
Recognition arm rotation is limited to a single horizontal pivot for training interaction.
Unreadable printed labels are replaced by generated semantic training labels.
Basket, red logbook, loose cables and human hands are separate scene props and excluded from kiosk geometry.
